page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

The underlying AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. In performance testing, the instance demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling shows some limitations, as Geekbench multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression results fall into the bottom 25%.

Memory performance is mixed; while the PassMark memory score and large-block write bandwidth are average, read-only memory bandwidth benchmarks are weak. Due to the lack of local storage and lower database and Redis SET performance, this instance is less suited for heavy database operations or high-throughput web serving. It is best utilized for compute-bound, single-threaded tasks, text processing, or lightweight batch processing workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and AVX-512 instruction support without requiring large memory footprints or local disk I/O.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor at 2.7 GHz. Running on the KVM hypervisor, it provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with no local storage or GPU resources. The instance supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration. Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, placing in the top 25%, while multi-core scaling and memory read bandwidth are weaker, landing in the bottom 25%. With a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for dedicated compute workloads that do not demand high memory capacity or local storage. It is best suited for single-threaded processing, text manipulation, and lightweight compute tasks.
